Hi Alex — quick technical + pricing notes from Redwood SE perspective: 

1) Pricing flavors (short):
- Hosted: no commit, standard per-token billing, simplest to start for POC.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, commit-based discounts (material for sustained >500M tokens/month).
- Private: VPC/on-prem options for customers with strict networking/compliance needs; pricing includes platform fee + infra.

2) Effective unit economics drivers
- Sequence length & model architecture: longer avg seq -> higher tokens per request; generation-heavy workloads increase token burn.
- Caching/prefix reuse: for repeated prompts or static context, KV/prefix caching reduces net tokens served; can drop effective unit cost 15–35% depending on reuse.
- Batching & compaction: efficient batching reduces milliseconds per-token cost and lowers $$/1M at scale.

3) Ballpark benchmarking (very rough, for sizing only)
- OpenAI (public/experimental blended): ~$18–28 / 1M tokens (depends on model).
- Anthropic (public): ~$16–26 / 1M tokens.
- Redwood Hosted (open-models, quantized + caching assumptions): ~$9–12 / 1M tokens.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved commit, model selection + quantization): ~$5–8 / 1M tokens (for moderately large commits and with caching/batching assumptions).

Caveats: these are illustrative ranges — the final number depends on model selection (open vs proprietary), avg sequence length, response length, and commit level. We’ll run a tailored cost model once we have the month-by-month numbers you populate.

I’ve attached a short benchmarking note (redwood-benchmarking-notes.pdf) that shows the assumptions used for these ranges (seq lengths, cache hit rates, model mix).
